abstract: One directory tree of Markdown items plus exactly one agsc.config.json: the unit of publication and of conformance.
text:
A **Bundle** is one directory tree of Markdown items plus exactly one `agsc.config.json`. It is the unit of publication and the unit of conformance: one repository is one Bundle.

Items live at `content/<type-plural>/<slug>.md`. The Bundle root document, `content/index.md`, carries `spec_version`, `okf_version`, `title`, `description` and `base`, and is not itself an item. The Bundle IRI is the site base followed by `/`, and in the graph the Bundle is an `asc:Bundle`, the concept scheme every Concept is in.
title: Bundle

abstract: A navigational grouping of items. Membership is authored on the item, and nesting is expressed as membership.
text:
A **Cluster** groups items for navigation. Membership is authored on the item, in `clusters[]`, never on the cluster file; the first cluster listed is the item's primary cluster.

In the graph a Cluster is an `asc:Cluster`, a subclass of `skos:Collection`, and membership is `skos:member`. A cluster may name at most one parent with `broader`, which is exported as membership of the parent, never as `skos:broader`.
title: Cluster

abstract: A unit of knowledge in a Bundle, qualified by kind: pattern, taxonomy, explainer, principle, decision, spec, task, term or architecture.
text:
A **Concept** is a unit of knowledge in a Bundle. Its `kind` says what sort of knowledge it is: a pattern, a taxonomy, an explainer, a principle, a decision, a spec, a task, a term or an architecture.

In the graph a Concept is an `asc:Concept`, a subclass of `skos:Concept`, and carries `skos:inScheme` the Bundle, its title as `skos:prefLabel` and its description as `skos:definition`. Every term on this site is a Concept of kind `term`.
title: Concept

abstract: A recorded occurrence, such as a session, a run or an incident, with a start instant, an actor and an outcome.
text:
An **Episode** records something that happened: a session, a run or an incident. It carries `started`, `actor` and an `outcome` of `success`, `partial` or `failure`, and may carry `ended`, `refs[]` and token accounting in `usage{}`.

In the graph an Episode is an `asc:Episode`, a subclass of `prov:Activity`. Knowledge distilled from Episodes is written as a Lesson.
title: Episode

abstract: A declared set of checks that a change must pass, at level L1 or L2. Its runs are recorded as episodes.
text:
A **Gate** declares the checks a change must pass. It carries a `level` of `L1` (schema and links) or `L2` (which adds provenance, determinism and review), and may say how it is enforced.

In the graph a Gate is an `asc:Gate`, a subclass of `prov:Plan`; its runs are Episodes.
title: Gate

abstract: Procedures for publishing and reading a node, each step naming the rule or the check that proves it.
text: Procedures for publishing and reading a node, each step naming the rule or the check that proves it.
title: Guides

abstract: Generated output: the file map a valid composition of selected items produces. A Harness is never authored.
text:
A **Harness** is generated output. A composition takes an ordered selection of item slugs and the resolved graph and produces a verdict plus a Harness: files of seven kinds, written outside `content/`, that describe a system built from the selected items: a record of the selection and its closure in canonical JSON (`harness.jsonld`, not an RDF JSON-LD document), a context file for agents, a Structurizr model, a Mermaid diagram, an arc42 skeleton, one decision record per selected item and one skill file per selected Procedure.

In agentic systems the word *harness* names the frame an agent runs inside: the scaffolding that embeds the agents and dictates the rules they follow. The specification uses the word in that sense, with one precision: a Harness here is that frame written down as files, not the running process. A runtime such as GABBE, kaiban-distributed, CrewAI or LangGraph can start from these files or render them into its own form; such a rendering is never part of the Harness itself, and none ships with the reference engine at 1.0. In the ontology a Harness is a plan (`asc:Harness`, a kind of `prov:Plan`).

A composition needs no network, key or server. A Harness is never authored and never stored as an item, and an invalid composition yields no Harness at all.
title: Harness

abstract: One Markdown file with YAML frontmatter whose type is concept, episode, procedure, lesson, cluster or gate.
text:
An **item** is one `.md` file with YAML frontmatter whose `type` is one of `concept`, `episode`, `procedure`, `lesson`, `cluster` or `gate`.

"Item" is a term of the specification only: the ontology has no common superclass for the six types, because an Activity is not an Entity. Every item carries `type`, `title` and `prov`; its slug is the file stem and the last path segment of its IRI, and a slug is permanent.
title: Item

abstract: Knowledge distilled from one or more episodes, carrying a severity of info, warn or block.
text:
A **Lesson** is knowledge distilled from one or more Episodes. It carries a `severity` of `info`, `warn` or `block` and should name the Episode it derives from; its body uses the headings `Lesson`, `Evidence` and `Check before`.

In the graph a Lesson is an `asc:Lesson`, a subclass of `asc:Concept`: failure knowledge is kept as items, not in a separate error file.
title: Lesson

abstract: A typed relation between two items of one Bundle, written as a frontmatter key whose values are slugs.
text:
A **Link** is a typed relation between two items of the same Bundle. It is written as a frontmatter array under one of fourteen keys: the nine core keys `related`, `broader`, `narrower`, `uses`, `requires`, `excludes`, `derived-from`, `contradicts` and `supersedes`, and the five Mode-2 keys `implements`, `verifies`, `covers`, `blocked-by` and `decided-by`.

Each value is a slug. A Link never crosses Bundles: a reference to another node is a citation in `sources[]`.
title: Link

abstract: Generated context about the current state of a Bundle, such as counts and last build. NOW is never an item.
text:
**NOW** is generated context: counts, the last build, stale items, open Lessons and monthly spend. It is produced from stored state only and is never hand-edited; a section whose input is absent is omitted, not guessed.

NOW is never an item.
title: NOW

abstract: A plan a reader can execute: a trigger, steps and checks. Procedures are published in skill packs, one pack per cluster.
text:
A **Procedure** is a plan a reader can execute. It may carry `when`, a one-line trigger saying when it applies, and `inputs[]`; its body uses the headings `When`, `Steps` and `Checks`. Procedures are published in skill packs, one pack per cluster holding the cluster's published items, and the pack takes its description from the cluster; a skill imported from elsewhere arrives as a Procedure whose `when` is that skill's description.

In the graph a Procedure is an `asc:Procedure`, a subclass of `prov:Plan`.
title: Procedure

abstract: Turn an existing CMS, wiki or static-site export into a conforming Level-0 node without running an engine.
text:
## Checks

- The discovery document parses as I-JSON and `linkset` is its only top-level member.
- Every `href` is absolute, and the targets within one relation are ordered by `href`.
- `/llms.txt` begins with the H1 and lists every published item exactly once.
- Your conformance claim names Level 0, the `spec_version` and the vector areas you ran.
title: Publish a Level-0 node

abstract: Turn an existing CMS, wiki or static-site export into a conforming Level-0 node without running an engine.
text:
## Steps

1. Choose the site base, an absolute `https:` URL. Every item IRI is the base, the type folder and the slug, with a trailing slash.
2. Export each piece of knowledge as `content/<type-plural>/<slug>.md` with frontmatter carrying at least `type`, `title` and `prov`. `prov` is required at every Level; an item without it is `AGSC-E501` (AGSC-10-02, case `fm-0004`).
3. Write `content/index.md` with `spec_version`, `okf_version`, `title`, `description` and `base`.
4. Publish `/graph.jsonld`, the JSON-LD view of the items.
5. Publish `/llms.txt` in the byte layout of AGSC-06-13a: the title as an H1, the provenance comment, the description, then one section per cluster.
6. Publish `/.well-known/knowledge-linkset`: a link set whose only top-level member is `linkset`, holding one link context anchored at the base. Level 0 omits every `digest` and `agsc-*` attribute.
7. Serve that file as `application/linkset+json` with the `profile` parameter, or send a `Link` header with `rel="profile"`.
8. Serve the public artefacts with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, and put a `describedby` link to the discovery document in the head of your pages.
9. Check the discovery document with an implementation of AGSC-09-93, such as `tools/validate-wellknown` of the reference implementation, or run the Level-0 vectors in your own language.
title: Publish a Level-0 node

abstract: Turn an existing CMS, wiki or static-site export into a conforming Level-0 node without running an engine.
text:
## When

You have content in a CMS, a wiki or a static-site generator and want people and agents to discover and read it as a node, without adopting an engine. Level 0 asks for static files only.
title: Publish a Level-0 node

abstract: The items recorded against the release candidates were applied, the whole vector set was run with the reference engine, and version 1.0.0 was tagged, with the reference engine's own conformance claim.
text: Version 1.0.0 of the specification was released and tagged, and with it the reference engine published its own conformance claim: a claim needs a green run of that Level's whole vector set at a released version, which a release candidate is not (AGSC-10-05).
title: Release version 1.0.0 of the specification

abstract: The items recorded against the release candidates were applied, the whole vector set was run with the reference engine, and version 1.0.0 was tagged, with the reference engine's own conformance claim.
text:
## What done means

- Every item recorded against the release candidates is either applied, with a dated amendment note on each changed rule, or moved to a later version with a reason.
- A vector found wrong is withdrawn and replaced by a new one, never edited (AGSC-00-16).
- The reference engine passes every required vector of the Level-3 set, and the report is published with the claim.
- The specification's tag and the engine's tag are pushed on one commit by the maintainer.
title: Release version 1.0.0 of the specification

abstract: The items recorded against the release candidates were applied, the whole vector set was run with the reference engine, and version 1.0.0 was tagged, with the reference engine's own conformance claim.
text:
## Who does it

The maintainer decides and tags. Anyone may propose a correction to a rule through the forge; an agent may prepare a proposal, and a person reviews it.
title: Release version 1.0.0 of the specification

abstract: An external work cited by an item, written inline as a sources[] entry and published under a fragment IRI.
text:
A **Source** is an external work an item cites. It has no file of its own: it is written inline as an entry of `sources[]`, whose `resource` is a web URL or a channel identifier.

In the graph each entry becomes an `asc:Source`, a subclass of `prov:Entity`, at the IRI `<item-IRI>#source-<n>`, and the item points to it with `asc:source`.
title: Source
